claim: vLLM's KV-event publishing mechanism was deliberately designed as a separate, decoupled pub/sub 'fire and forget' sink alongside the Scheduler, not merged into the existing KV Connector API used for actual KV-tensor transfer (which requires retry/ack semantics at ~100MB/s).
stance_target: why vLLM KV events are a distinct low-bandwidth channel from the KV-transfer Connector API
scope_conditions: vLLM RFC discussion, Apr 2025, resolved Nov 2025
quoted_support: KV-Transfer handles 100MB/s tensor w/ retry and ack, and CPU -> GPU transfer. KV Event publishing is low bandwidth publishing, pub/sub w/ fire and forget (we can add a simple ack)

claim: NVIDIA Dynamo's own kv_router (publisher.rs / indexer.rs in github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo) predates and closely parallels vLLM's native KVEvents design, using the same publisher/global-prefix-tree-indexer split.
stance_target: prior art for KV-event-based distributed cache indexing
quoted_support: Here is our publisher (this has python bindings): https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/lib/llm/src/kv_router/publisher.rs / Here is our consumer (also has python bindings): https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/lib/llm/src/kv_router/indexer.rs

claim: IBM Research explicitly frames KVEvents (internal engine-state visibility) as complementary to, not a replacement for, the KV Connector API's external-storage-locality visibility, with a stated roadmap to combine both for fine-grained KV-aware routing.
stance_target: relationship between KVEvents and KV Connector API in a combined routing architecture
scope_conditions: vLLM RFC discussion, Apr 2025, IBM Research perspective (vMaroon, later author of the Red Hat llm-d KV-cache-routing blog)
quoted_support: It makes sense to start with the two pieces decoupled, but streamlining the API is probably a necessary followup... combining vLLM-internal insights with node-local indexing is key to enabling fine-grained, KV-aware request routing.

claim: Storage/medium generalization of KV-block events (e.g., a block backed by remote storage like Redis/S3) was explicitly raised in the original design discussion and later materialized as the medium field (GPU/CPU/STORAGE) in the shipped BlockStored event.
stance_target: extensibility of KV events to non-standard storage backends
scope_conditions: vLLM RFC discussion, Apr 2025, tracked forward to shipped kv_events.py
quoted_support: how does this design handle the case where the KV cache is stored in a remote storage, like Reddis? ... We could just treat the storage as extra KVCache and emit the same BlockStored event.
